newsitem.title: ITALY: SOCCER-CHAMPIONS JUVENTUS READY TO TOPPLE LEADERS INTER-MILAN.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-CHAMPIONS JUVENTUS READY TO TOPPLE LEADERS INTER-MILAN.

text.p: New Italian league leaders Inter-Milan face their first serious test of the season when they travel to Turin to face European champions Juventus on Sunday night.
Five games into the new season, Inter lead by just one point from a quartet of second placed sides - Parma, AS Roma, Bologna, and Juventus.
Inter might be in front but they have not impressed in picking up nine of their 10 points against Serie A also-rans , Udinese, Perugia, Atalanta and Piacenza.
In a midweek UEFA Cup home tie, Inter again struggled to beat the modest Austrian side Casino Graz 1-0, thanks to an 81st minute goal from French defender Jocelyn Angloma.
Inter defender Salvatore Fresi argues that, media criticism notwithstanding, being on top of the league brings a psychological advantage.

"The difference between this season and last is tangible, opponents look on us with more respect. Let's hope it goes well in Turin. The longer we remain on top, the more respect we'll earn, the more opponents will fear us," he told reporters.
Recent tradition is against Inter since their last league win against Juventus came in the 1992-1993 season when they pulled off a 3-1 and 2-0 home and away double.
On Sunday, Inter will also be without their influential English midfielder Paul Ince, currently suspended.

Inter and Ince contest a two-day ban at a Friday disciplinary commission sitting but even if they win their appeal, Ince can hope for only a one-day reduction at best, following his sending off against Piacenza last Saturday.
Inter's English coach Roy Hodgson will replace Ince with Swiss midfielder Ciriaco Sforza, alongside Argentine Javier Zanetti, Frenchman Youri Djorkaeff and Dutchman Aron Winter.
In attack, Maurizio Ganz may be preferred to Chilean Ivan Zamorano as a partner for Marco Branca.

Juventus, too, come into the match after a week of mixed fortunes which saw them held to a 1-1 Champions League draw away to Austrian side Rapid Vienna on Wednesday, five days after a 2-1 league defeat by Vicenza.
Goalkeeper Angelo Peruzzi and French midfielder Zinedine Zidane, who both missed the Rapid encounter, are expected to return for the clash with Inter.

Croat Alen Boksic and Italian Michele Padovano will form the attack while Zidane regains his place alongside compatriot Didier Deschamps and Angelo Di Livio, probably at the expense of Serb Vladimir Jugovic.
Juventus's stylish striker, Alessandro Del Piero, who has been out of action since sustaining an ankle injury last month, is expected to come on as a second half substitute.
